citeAs: Badertdinov, I., Golubev, A., Nekrashevich, M., Shevtsov, A., Karasik, S., Andriushchenko, A., Trofimova, M., Litvintseva, D., & Yangel, B. (2025). SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents. 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025).
creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel (Nebius)
description: SWE-rebench is a public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, suitable for reinforcement learning of SWE agents at scale.
name: SWE-rebench
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For Task Complexity, the fine-tuned model achieved 81% accuracy and a weighted F1-score of 0.82. For Test Patch Correctness, the model achieved 67% accuracy. For Issue Clarity, it achieved 79% accuracy.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We fine-tune Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct using annotations from SWE-bench Verified. For each of the over 3,800 examples, the model receives the issue description, the canonical solution patch, and the test patch as input. It is then prompted to predict one of three binary quality labels: Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, or Test Patch Correctness.
rai:dataBiases: The initial release of SWE-rebench is limited exclusively to Python, restricting its immediate applicability to other language ecosystems.
rai:dataCollection: We download raw input data from multiple origins, merge them, and perform preliminary filtering. The primary sources for our data are GitHub Archive and GitHub. We then link issues with pull requests that mention resolving them in their title or description.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The primary sources for our data are GitHub Archive and GitHub. We download approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025. These originate from over 30,000 repositories that feature permissive licenses and where Python constitutes over 75% of the codebase lines of code.
rai:dataLimitations: The fully automated pipeline may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue. This can lead to lower absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks. The initial release of SWE-rebench is limited exclusively to Python.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For each selected pull request, the overall patch is divided into two components: a solution patch, containing changes to non-test files intended to address the issue, and a test patch, comprising only changes to test files.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We group these task instances by project versions inferred from git tag outputs, normalizing versions to major.minor format. We employ an agentless approach to generate candidate environment setup instructions.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: SWE-rebench uses an automated pipeline for a continuous supply of fresh tasks. The leaderboard is continuously updated.
rai:dataSocialImpact: It may accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering. This progress brings potential risks, such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities.
rai:dataUseCases: Designed to train and benchmark agents in diverse executable environments, particularly suitable for reinforcement learning-based approaches.
